summary: Agent-safety benchmarks demonstrate substantial failures and attack success in tool-using settings. They strongly support hard boundaries, but benchmark attack rates should not be read as incident rates for a specific production deployment.

items.text: ToolEmu (ICLR 2024) emulates risky tool-use scenarios; human evaluation judged 68.8% of the generated failure cases to be valid and realistic, motivating adversarial evaluation before granting broad action authority. This percentage is a validity judgment on discovered failures, not an overall agent failure rate.
AgentDojo (NeurIPS 2024) benchmarks prompt-injection attacks and defenses in realistic tool-using tasks, showing the tension between utility and security under untrusted data.
Agent Security Bench (ICLR 2025) evaluates multiple attack and defense categories and reports high attack success for evaluated agents, while noting limited defense effectiveness.
